title: Add a built-in Standard document type to the story-convention profile (DEC-167 (3))
description:
opum-doc DEC-167 clause (3) (accepted; landed via opum-ai/opum-doc#770), operator-approved first-party, routed to lore-cli through opum-agent. Read at source: "Each standard is written as type: Reference until lore ships a built-in Standard type, then its type line flips (operator's choice A). lore-cli adds Standard to its built-in story-convention profile, with required sections matching (2), in the next lore release."

Spec: name Standard, slug standard. Required body sections, in this order: Purpose, Scope, Rules, Enforcement, Exceptions, Related. No required fields beyond the base set; status uses the existing draft | stable | deprecated enum. A built-in template for `lore new --type Standard` carrying those six headings. Surfaces: `lore types` lists it, `lore schema export` emits standard.schema.json, and the default profile's docs and tests are updated. Additive: no existing kind's version is bumped, and no release is cut or published for this (it rides the next lore/quest pair cut).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The story-convention profile declares a Standard type (slug standard) whose required sections are Purpose, Scope, Rules, Enforcement, Exceptions, Related in that order, with no required fields beyond the base set; status stays the existing draft|stable|deprecated enum.
`lore new --type Standard` scaffolds a document from a built-in template carrying the six headings in order.
`lore types` lists Standard and `lore schema export` emits .lore/schemas/standard.schema.json.
The change is additive (no existing kind version bumped) and the default profile docs and tests are updated; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.

plan: 1. Add Standard to storyConventionProfile.types (profile.ts): slug standard, sections in order, no extra fields.
2. Add STANDARD_TEMPLATE (template.ts) with the six headings in order; register it in BUILTIN_TEMPLATES.
3. Update tests that pin the built-in vocabulary/type list (type-vocabulary, schema-export, types, new, template, profile) and add Standard coverage.
4. Update the default-profile docs (cli-surface / okf-conformance / etc.).
5. bun test + bun run lore check exit 0; branch, PR into dev, required checks.
finalSummary: LCLI-687 (opum-doc DEC-167 (3)). Added the built-in Standard document type to the story-convention profile, additive — no existing kind's version bumped. PR opum-ai/lore-cli#510 (squash 1c5159d2). Name Standard, slug standard; required sections Purpose, Scope, Rules, Enforcement, Exceptions, Related, in order; no fields beyond the shared base set; status keeps the base draft|stable|deprecated enum; declared on every OKF version like the other lore-only types (Constitution, Constants). STANDARD_TEMPLATE gives `lore new Standard` the six headings in order (the type is a positional, so the spec's "lore new --type Standard" is that call). The surfaces follow from the profile: `lore types` lists Standard, and `lore schema export` emits .lore/schemas/standard.schema.json (count now 11) — the committed schemas were regenerated, their x-lore-generator profileDigest moving with the profile. One choice DERIVED from the design and flagged in the PR for opum-doc: Standard scaffolds into docs/standards/ (added to TYPE_DIRECTORIES), from DEC-167 (2) placing standards there and the many-instance plural convention (Epic/Arc/Spec/Runbook); the spec named no directory. Verified: a focused test/lcli687-standard-type.test.ts (7 cases incl. the profile declaration, template headings, `lore new Standard` end-to-end, `lore types`, and required-section enforcement by presence); a valid-wing okf fixture; the built-in vocabulary lists updated across nine test files; and the docker e2e harness's exact schema-count/file-list assertion updated (11, not 10) after the required docker e2e context caught it. Gates: CI green on the PR head, bun test 4967 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, bun run lore check 0 errors / 0 warnings, typecheck and biome clean.
